blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it
R-accessibility-1 (Field errors are conveyed by colour only, with no text and no programmatic state) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
`field--invalid`, a red border (`#e5484d`); the list of errors at the top of
the page is removed, since the red border already shows where the problem
is. No message text is added, to keep the form compact.
findings.recommendation: Screen reader users and colour-blind users cannot tell which field is invalid or why: a screen reader user tabs out of the postcode field with `ABC`, the border turns red, and nothing is announced; on the field, only its label is read. This fails WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color, 3.3.1 Error Identification and 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value, and the removal of the error list leaves no text alternative anywhere. Keep the red border, but add for each invalid field a visible text message next to it (say what is wrong and how to fix it, WCAG 3.3.3), associate it with `aria-describedby`, and set `aria-invalid="true"` while the field is invalid. Update the spec's requirement and scenarios ("the field's border turns red", "the border returns to grey") so they require the message and the invalid state, not just the colour, and add them to task 1.2's tests.
findings.title: Field errors are conveyed by colour only, with no text and no programmatic state

findings.evidence: Each field validates on `blur`. An invalid field gets the class
findings.recommendation: Validation only runs on blur, and the error list at the top is removed, but the plan does not say what happens when the form is submitted with invalid or never-visited fields. A keyboard user who presses Enter on the submit button with an empty required field they never focused gets no blur validation and no list: either nothing happens or fields turn red off screen, with no announcement and focus left on the button (WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification, 2.4.3 Focus Order, 4.1.3 Status Messages). Specify the submit path: validate every field on submit, move focus to the first invalid field (or to an error summary linking to each field), and add a scenario for it in the spec.
findings.title: Nothing tells a keyboard or screen reader user where the errors are on submit
